messages:
noa: Post-sync note: I've been pulling together heuristics for onboarding precision profiles without forcing full eval runs. Want feedback on the quick-path approach.
felix: curious. Quick-path = what, exactly? tiny shadow runs + model-catalog priors?
noa: exactly. Steps: (1) sample N requests (configurable, default 2k) for a short window, (2) compute prompt fingerprint distribution, (3) map fingerprints to catalog delta priors per bitpath, (4) aggregate weighted mean+variance and return a recommended profile + a confidence band.
tara: 2k seems small for some long-tail tasks. can we bootstrap with smaller N and adaptive sampling?
noa: yes. adaptive: start at 500, compute bootstrap CI; if CI width > threshold then continue sampling up to max (10k). This keeps quick on small stable workloads.
felix: how do we bucket fingerprints? full-fingerprint cardinality could explode.
noa: we use locality-sensitive hashing into ~256 buckets per-endpoint, computed on canonicalized prompt features (length, token-ngrams, system-prompt hash). That gives stable buckets that align with catalog anchor stats.
ara: minor nit: system prompts can change and invalidate buckets. need to include a version tag in the endpoint profile.
noa: agreed. endpoint_profile_version is part of the recommendation and locked into ledger rows.
infra-bot: Reminder: any sampling must be safe w.r.t PII. Please run the PII-scan hook on sample sets.
tara: what about the math? how do we combine priors and observed frequencies? Bayes-ish?
noa: simple conjugate update: treat catalog priors as Normal(mu0, sigma0^2) per-bitpath per-bucket, observed sample mean mu_obs with variance s^2/n, posterior mean = weighted average. We avoid heavy ML so it's explainable.
felix: sounds good. how do we present uncertainty to customers? a single number is risky.
noa: UI shows recommended target_quality_loss_pct as mean and confidence_band (mean +/- 2*std). We also show an "uncertainty_label": low/medium/high which is derived from relative width.
tara: telemetry: need to emit sample_size, buckets_covered_pct, catalog_prior_age, and whether we used heuristic fallback.
ops-bot: Ops note: ensure recommendations include a suggested canary plan (percentages + duration) generated from uncertainty_label. Low uncertainty -> faster ramp.
felix: runtime side: if customers accept recommended profile, we still need runtime admission control and a simple circuit-breaker if degscore jumps.
noa: plan: recommended guardrail fields include max_inflight_lowbit_ratio and auto_revert_threshold_pct (degscore drift). default conservative values generated by the heuristic engine.
tara: what about multi-model endpoints where routing mixes model families with different delta priors?
noa: we weight catalog priors by actual runtime routing percentages observed during sampling. if routing changes much post-onboard, recommendation invalidates and we flag for re-run.
felix: auditing: ledger must include the sample snapshot id so we can recompute the recommendation. Also keep seed for the LSH buckets.
noa: yes ledger will store sample_snapshot_id, lsh_seed, profile_version, and the catalog_prior_revision used. Retention per audit rules.
infra-bot: CI: there's an infra PR to add sample_snapshot metadata storage (#1178). Tests pending.
tara: edge case: adversarial prompts or extremely rare anchors. If bucket frequency < 0.1% we should mark as low support and not base aggressive recommendations on them.
noa: we'll floor contributions from tiny buckets and include a fallback to global model-average priors.
felix: final thought: for customers who can't run sampling, provide a conservative canned-recommendation based on model-family + common workload heuristics.
noa: agreed. that will be the "fast opt-in" path in console. longer-term we can automate periodic re-sampling and tune profiles.
tara: who owns the spike to implement this?
felix: I'll take infra + sampling collector. noa you own the recommendation engine and UI bits. I'll open a PR for the snapshot storage.
ops-bot: scheduled: sampling-spike-job #812 queued (ETA ~3h).
noa: thanks. I'll draft an RFC appendix with the math and the privacy checklist and post link when ready. :thumbsup:
